Description

Active ERK limits its own activation within minutes by phosphorylating the kinases above it. In RAF1 it phosphorylates five of six serines that turn the kinase off after stimulation, and in BRAF four serines and threonines [1, 2]. The hyperphosphorylated RAF no longer binds active RAS, BRAF no longer pairs with RAF1, and RAF stops responding to a second stimulus [1, 2]. It is not degraded: protein phosphatase 2A, helped by the prolyl isomerase Pin1, removes the feedback phosphates and returns RAF to a state in which it can signal again [1, 2]. This cycle of feedback phosphorylation and recycling sets how long a signal from the membrane lasts [3]. Another study found that ERK phosphorylation of three of the RAF1 sites (Ser289, Ser296 and Ser301) after EGF sustains RAF1 activity, so the effect of these sites may depend on the cell and the stimulus [4].

References
